major_projects.title: NAKHWA
major_projects.short_desc: NAKHWA is a smart boat safety and monitoring system designed using IoT, GPS, and LTE technologies. The system uses a custom ESP32 board integrated with the EC200U GSM/GPS module for real-time boat tracking and cloud connectivity.
major_projects.summary: NAKHWA is an advanced smart boat safety and monitoring system designed to enhance maritime safety using IoT, GPS, and LTE communication technologies. The system is built around a custom ESP32-based board integrated with the EC200U GSM/GPS module, enabling real-time location tracking and cloud connectivity. It incorporates multiple sensors including the MPU6050 to measure the boat's pitch and roll for capsizing detection, a flame sensor, temperature sensor, and gas sensor to monitor onboard safety conditions. To reduce false fire alerts caused by environmental factors such as sunlight affecting the flame sensor, the system intelligently cross-verifies data using temperature and gas sensor readings before triggering a fire alert. An SOS emergency button is also integrated, allowing crew members to instantly send emergency notifications to the control center during critical situations. GPS coordinates and sensor data are transmitted over LTE and stored in a Supabase cloud database for real-time monitoring and analytics. A dedicated live dashboard interface displays vessel status, alerts, activity monitoring, and boat locations on a map, enabling authorities or operators to continuously monitor fleet safety and respond quickly during emergencies.

Sensing Layer: Continuously captures: latitude/longitude, roll angle (θ), acceleration (m/s²), angular velocity (°/s)
Temperature (°C), vessel speed (km/h or knots), flame/smoke status
Edge Processing Layer: Embedded Firmware — Real-time sensor interfacing, safety constraint evaluation, alert classification, and communication control
VSCode — Firmware development, compilation, and deployment onto the ESP32
Multi-parameter sensor fusion with configurable safety thresholds (roll threshold, max speed) pushed remotely from the central dashboard
Communication & Control Layer: GSM/GPRS — Transmits sensor data and alerts to the central IoT dashboard; SMS for SOS events
Apache Kafka Streaming Framework — Scalable, low-latency event streaming pipeline for centralized multi-vessel monitoring

Sensor Node: GNSS–GSM Module (EC200U) — Real-time geographic positioning, ground speed estimation, heading, and wireless data transmission
IMU (MPU6050) — Roll and pitch angle computation for vessel stability and motion analysis
Temperature Sensor — Onboard thermal condition monitoring for fire-risk assessment
Smoke Sensor + IR Sensor — Combined combustion detection (smoke + infrared radiation)
SOS Push Button — Manual emergency signaling
Custom ESP32 PCB — All peripherals integrated onto a single board (KiCad designed)

major_projects.title: NEXUS Architecture — Quadranode Rover
major_projects.short_desc: A rugged, fault-tolerant solar-powered rover with a distributed 4-node ESP32 architecture, STM32 RTOS failover, and Raspberry Pi 4B as master server with remote access via Tailscale VPN.
major_projects.summary: The Quadranode Rover is a distributed IoT system designed for rugged outdoor operation. Four ESP32 microcontrollers each own a dedicated function — sensing, actuation, GPS/LTE, and camera. An STM32 Nucleo board running RTOS acts as a hardware failover layer, capable of taking over any failed ESP32 node. A Raspberry Pi 4B serves as the central server, aggregating data from all nodes over MQTT (Mosquitto broker), and exposing remote access through Tailscale VPN. GitHub SSH enables over-the-air firmware updates. The rover is solar powered with dual current/voltage monitoring — one pair tracking solar input, the other tracking real-time power consumption — and an internal thermal management system with auto-cutoff for thermal protection.

Master Node (RPi 4B): Mosquitto MQTT broker for all inter-node communication
Tailscale VPN for secure remote access from anywhere
GitHub SSH for OTA firmware updates to all nodes
Central dashboard aggregating all node telemetry data
Sensor Node Firmware: Reads BH1750, MPU6050, 4× ultrasonic, 2× INA current/voltage pairs, DS18B20
Triggers cooling fan or automatic power cutoff on thermal spike
Actuation Node Firmware: Controls relays, motor drivers, and servos for rover movement and articulation
GPS/LTE Node Firmware: EC200u module for real-time GPS position and LTE uplink
Streams location to RPi for live map tracking
Camera Node Firmware: Pan-tilt servo for 270° field of view coverage
RTOS Failover (STM32): STM32 Nucleo + RTOS monitors all ESP32 nodes
Takes over any crashed node via RTOS task scheduling
LoRa fallback communication when LTE is unavailable

Raspberry Pi 4B: Master server — runs Mosquitto broker, Tailscale VPN, and GitHub SSH agent
4× ESP32 Nodes: One per function: Sensor, Actuation, GPS/LTE, Camera
Each independently connected to RPi via MQTT over Wi-Fi/LTE
STM32 Nucleo + RTOS: Watchdog failover board — monitors all ESP32 nodes
Takes over a failed node's function via RTOS task scheduling
Power System: Solar input with dual INA current/voltage pairs — one for solar output, one for consumption monitoring
Thermal Management: Auto cooling fan on threshold breach; automatic power cutoff if temperature continues to rise
EC200u (GPS/LTE) + LoRa: Quectel EC200u for simultaneous GPS fix and 4G LTE uplink
LoRa module as long-range fallback when LTE is unavailable, managed by STM32 RTOS node

major_projects.title: Smart Digital Circuit Breaker
major_projects.short_desc: Developed an IoT-based smart digital circuit breaker using ESP32 and FreeRTOS for real-time electrical monitoring and automated protection. Integrates multiple sensors, SSR relay control, cloud connectivity via Supabase, and a React live web dashboard for remote monitoring and control.
major_projects.summary: Designed and developed an advanced IoT-enabled digital circuit breaker capable of monitoring current, voltage, temperature, and gas levels in real time using an ESP32 microcontroller running FreeRTOS with 6 concurrent tasks. The system features automated circuit protection through 4-channel SSR relay control, offline hardware trip logic, gas leak emergency shutdown, and hysteresis-based relay switching for enhanced safety and stability. A scalable backend was built using Node.js and Supabase, enabling per-board configurable thresholds, AI-based risk scoring, and bidirectional cloud-to-device communication. A React-based industrial dark-theme dashboard was developed to visualize live sensor data, display real-time power charts, configure thresholds, and manually control relays remotely. A 16×2 LCD was integrated to provide live system status and safety alerts directly on the device.

ESP32 Firmware (FreeRTOS): Dual-core ESP32 architecture running 6 concurrent real-time tasks for sensing, safety, cloud communication, and display handling
Mutex-protected shared state synchronization using semaphores to ensure safe multi-core data access without race conditions
Hierarchical safety logic with hardware-level overcurrent and gas protection operating independently of cloud connectivity
Non-blocking DS18B20 temperature acquisition to avoid delays in critical task execution
Resilient cloud communication with automatic WiFi recovery, HTTPS JSON data transfer, AI risk scoring, and local fallback operation
Dashboard (React + Node.js): Futuristic industrial-themed React dashboard for real-time monitoring and control of the digital circuit protection system
Live monitoring of voltage, current, power consumption, temperature, gas levels, AI risk assessment, and cooling fan status
Interactive relay controls with real-time board status indicators and power flow visualization
Historical analytics featuring live power consumption graphs, event logs, and timestamp-based monitoring
Configurable threshold management for power, gas, and temperature limits with cloud-connected synchronization

Sensing Frontend: SCT-013-030 non-invasive CT sensor for current measurement
MQ gas sensor for leak detection
Processing & Display: 16×2 LCD for local power readout and safety alerts
4-channel SSR relay for automated circuit protection

major_projects.title: SafeTrack — Child Safety Tracking System
major_projects.short_desc: Real-time multi-device GPS tracking with geofencing, SOS alerting, and child safety mode. Built with ESP32 + Node.js backend + React dashboard + Supabase.
major_projects.summary: SafeTrack provides a real-time child safety and tracking solution using ESP32 and GPS technology to continuously stream live location data to a cloud dashboard via WiFi and WebSocket communication. It features SOS emergency alerting, where pressing a physical button triggers dashboard notifications, phone calls, and SMS alerts with a Google Maps location link using the SIM800L module. The platform supports geofencing — administrators can create safe zones on a map and receive instant alerts if a child exits the designated area. The system supports multiple devices simultaneously, with independent tracking, SOS monitoring, offline detection, and unique map markers for each device.

ESP32 Firmware: HTTPS POST handler with SSL/TLS secure client communication
Backend (Node.js + Render): Geofence engine using Turf.js for polygon containment checks
Frontend (React + Leaflet): Real-time WebSocket communication for live updates
Multiple map layer support (OSM / Bhuvan / Satellite)
Database (Supabase): Geofence zone polygon storage and breach detection logs

Hardware: ESP32-DevKit — Main MCU. Runs firmware, manages WiFi, reads GPS via UART2, controls button + buzzer via GPIO
NEO-7M GPS — Satellite positioning module. Outputs NMEA sentences at 9600 baud. Provides lat/lng, altitude, speed, fix quality
SIM800L GSM — 2G GSM/GPRS module. Makes voice calls and sends SMS to emergency numbers. Powered at 4V/2A
Push Button — SOS trigger. Wired between GPIO4 and GND with INPUT_PULLUP. Toggle press activates/deactivates SOS
Buzzer — Audio feedback on GPIO2. Plays Morse SOS pattern on alert, beeps on WiFi connect and GPS fix acquired
Power System: 3.7V 3000mAh Li-ion battery as primary power source
MT3608 step-up converter boosts battery voltage to stable 5V
6V 100mA solar panel integrated for portable solar charging
TP4056 charging module for safe Li-ion battery charging and power management

major_projects.title: NEX — Humanoid Robot Face
major_projects.short_desc: A humanoid robot face built with ESP32 and Raspberry Pi 4B, featuring real-time motion tracking via ultrasonic and PIR sensors, animated MAX7219 dot-matrix eyes, WS2812B audio-reactive LEDs, and a full ROS2 pipeline with remote visualization over Tailscale.
major_projects.wip_note: ESP32 sensor and actuator firmware is complete; ROS2 audio pipeline with wake word detection, Whisper STT, and Groq LLM integration is in progress. Vision node and YOLO object detection planned for next phase. ETA: Q4 2025.

major_projects.title: NEX Core — Wearable Biometric Hub
major_projects.short_desc: A wearable arc reactor-inspired biometric hub worn near the heart, integrating ECG, SpO2, temperature, and motion sensors with real-time Android visualization and humanoid robot health analysis sync.
major_projects.wip_note: Sensor fusion pipeline for ECG + SpO2 + temperature + MPU6050 is in active development. Android app graphs and saves all vitals. WS2812B activity-sync LED logic is being tuned. Humanoid proximity-based AI health briefing module is in early prototyping phase.

minor_projects.name: NEX-CAM
minor_projects.desc: NEX-CAM is an ESP32-CAM based wearable/handheld device combining motion sensing and camera functionality. It has two modes switched by physical buttons — emoji mode (MPU9250 IMU reads orientation and displays animated emoji faces on OLED based on tilt/motion) and camera mode (boots ESP32-CAM, connects to WiFi, and shows real-time status on OLED). Hardware stack: ESP32-CAM, MPU9250 IMU, SSD1306 OLED, two push buttons, and PCF8574 I²C GPIO expander. All I²C devices share a single bus on GPIO 13/14.

minor_projects.name: Audio Visualizer
minor_projects.desc: ESP32-based Audio Monitoring and Visualization System using three INMP MEMS microphones capturing surrounding sound from multiple directions. Processes real-time audio data on the ESP32 and visualizes live waveforms, FFT spectrum analysis, microphone intensity levels, and sound direction on an OLED display as well as a custom web dashboard.

minor_projects.name: Mini Oscilloscope
minor_projects.desc: Mini Digital Storage Oscilloscope (DSO) using Arduino Nano capable of capturing and visualizing electrical waveforms on a 0.96-inch OLED. Features real-time signal sampling, waveform processing, trigger handling, and input protection (resistor dividers, Zener clamping). Four push buttons and 10k potentiometer for menu navigation and scaling. Portable power management using 3.7V Li-ion battery, TP4056 charging module, and MT3608 step-up converter.

minor_projects.name: Environment Monitoring System
minor_projects.desc: IoT-based Environmental Monitoring System using ESP32 integrating MQ Gas Sensor, PM2.5 Sensor, BMP280, DHT22, BH1750 Light Sensor, and voltage/current sensing modules connected to a 12V solar panel. ESP32 hosts a live monitoring dashboard as a local web server. BH1750 measures solar intensity while V/I sensors monitor panel output — comparing both to evaluate solar efficiency. Integrated with Thynk Cloud for remote graphical monitoring.

minor_projects.name: Smart Study Desktop Lamp
minor_projects.desc: Smart Desktop Lamp using ESP32 integrating smart lighting, environmental monitoring, and wireless audio. 20×4 LCD shows real-time temperature, humidity, pressure, time, and date via Wi-Fi. Functions as a Bluetooth speaker with PAM amplifier and 2 speakers. Audio-reactive WS2812B RGB LED strip syncs animations and colors with music frequency and intensity. LDR-based automatic night lamp auto-activates below ambient light threshold. Powered by 3.7V Li-ion battery with TP4056 + MT3608.

minor_projects.name: Smart Weather Station
minor_projects.desc: DHT11 + BMP280 sensors pushing real-time humidity, temperature, and pressure to a webpage hosted on ESP32 acting as a local server. Dual charging support from a solar panel and a 12V adaptor keeps the station always powered.

minor_projects.name: RC BOT
minor_projects.desc: Long-range 10-channel RF Transmitter and Receiver System using nRF24L01 antenna modules for wireless communication and control. Built a multifunctional RC Rover capable of operating over an approximate range of 1 kilometre with stable real-time control.

minor_projects.name: Wi-Fi Controlled Car
minor_projects.desc: ESP32-based Wi-Fi controlled robotic car where the ESP32 acts as a local server hosting a wireless dashboard for real-time vehicle control. Features a dual steering mechanism combining Ackermann steering for smooth directional movement and rover-style differential steering for sharp turns. Powered by a 12V 8000mAh rechargeable battery.

minor_projects.name: Smart RGB Lamp
minor_projects.desc: NodeMCU-based Smart RGB Lamp using WS2812 addressable LEDs integrated with the WLED platform for wireless lighting control and customization. Controls brightness, colors, patterns, animations, and lighting effects through the WLED dashboard over Wi-Fi.
